Course Overview

Importance of Data Quality and Validation

  • Ensures accurate decision-making
  • Reduces errors and inconsistencies
  • Enhances data reliability and trust
  • Example:A healthcare provider uses high-quality patient data to ensure accurate diagnoses and treatment plans.

Data Quality

  • The condition of data based on factors such as accuracy, completeness, reliability and relevance.
  • Example: A retail company ensures product descriptions are accurate and complete to improve customer satisfaction.

Dimensions of Data Quality

  • Accuracy: Data correctly represents the real-world values.
    • Example:Correct customer addresses ensure successful deliveries.
  • Completeness: All required data is present.
    • Example:Complete financial records for accurate reporting.
  • Consistency: Data is consistent across different datasets.
    • Example:Consistent product information across online and offline channels.
  • Reliability/Validity: Data is dependable and trustworthy.
    • Example:Reliable employee data for payroll processing.
  • Timeliness: Data is up-to-date and available when needed.
    • Example:Real-time inventory data for stock management.
  • Uniqueness: Data should be distinct and not duplicated. No redundant information.
    • Example:Inaccurate customer insights for the bank if there are duplicated records.

Importance of High-Quality Data

  • Supports effective decision-making
  • Enhances operational efficiency
  • Improves customer satisfaction
  • Example:A bank uses high-quality transaction data to detect fraud.

Impact of poor Data Quality

  • Financial losses
  • Damage to reputation
  • Operational inefficiencies
  • Example:
    • logistics company faces delays due to inaccurate shipment data.
    • marketing campaign fails due to outdated customer contact information.
    • Incorrect customer addresses leading to delivery issues.
    • Incomplete financial records causing reporting errors.

Data Profiling & Monitoring

Example: E-commerce site monitoring product price anomalies in real time.

Real-World Data Quality Failures

Data Validation

  • Data is accurate, clean, and useful before processing
  • Example:Validating email addresses to ensure they follow the correct format.

Types of Data Validation

Validation Rules Examples

Validation rules come from:

  • Business requirements
  • Legal requirements
  • Data contracts
  • Common sense

Data Validation Techniques

  • Manual Validation: Human review of data.
    • Example:Manually checking survey responses for completeness.
  • Automated Validation: Using software tools to validate data.
    • Example:Using scripts to validate data formats in large datasets.

Pipeline Class Responsibilities

Validation Error!

  • case of a validation error and depending on what your business requirements are
  • ​> Send data back to production team
  • > Send log file back to production team containing vital information of the errors in the data

You are not responsible for cleaning the data, unless it is stated in the business requirements!

The log file contains the row and column of an error. If many of the same errors are observed, you can combine them in the log file.

Sending data back is sometimes rather difficult

- > Better solution: Make an 'error' folder, program uploads automatically wrong data files and corresponding log files to that folder, share the folder with your business client.
